//: Per-machine config for the bailiwick. Copy to .bailiwick-sync.json (gitignored) on each machine. Absent file => 'satellite' (safe default: never pushes to main, never owns telemetry).
//github_account: OPTIONAL. Multi-account machines (client laptops / VMs) only. Pins which logged-in 'gh' account the framework acts as — bootstrap's github MCP wiring AND sync_knowledge.sh's PR creation, both via hooks/gh_account.sh — overriding the access probe. 'github_account' = a blanket gh login; 'github_host' optionally overrides the API host. Use 'github_account_map' instead to pin per repo owner (owner -> gh login) — the deterministic form of your git URL-rewrite intent. The probe alone suffices when exactly one logged-in account can reach the repo; pin here when several can (or the probe warns 'ambiguous'). Leave empty/{} to disable.
//curate: OPTIONAL. 'deidentify': true forces every /curate promotion into de-identified mode — no client/project identifiers are ever stored (scope forced to generic, no clients/<id>/ files, org names/ids/project associations stripped at ingest), keeping only the reusable 'how it was solved'. Leave false for the normal model (client detail routed to clients/<id>/). Per-run override: '/curate --sanitized'.
//capture_backup: OPTIONAL encrypted off-machine backup of the dirty zone (.bailiwick-outputs/) so un-curated captures survive disk loss. Only CIPHERTEXT leaves the machine; the gpg private key never does. Disabled by default. 'repo' must be a DEDICATED PRIVATE repo (not the framework repo, not a client repo). 'gpg_recipients' = public key fingerprint(s); the matching private key lives only on the machine that runs /curate. 'confidentiality_ack' must be true to back up data that may include client material — enabling it asserts your engagement terms permit it.
